sections.heading: Roof Repair, Roof Replacement, or Roof Installation? The 25% Rule for Montclair Homeowners

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Once damage covers more than about 25% of the roof, replacement usually makes more sense than another repair. In New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of the roof area within 12 months also needs a permit on any building but a detached one- or two-family home, under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and a full roof replacement needs a building permit under the Uniform Construction Code on most buildings, while a detached one- or two-family reroof counts as ordinary maintenance. Confirm with the Montclair construction office before work.

Not automatically. Architectural asphalt shingles last approximately 20 to 30 years on average, and a basic three-tab roof in Montclair often needs replacement after 15 to 20 years, so a 20-year-old roof that inspects well may need only roof repair. Slate roofs can last for decades when properly installed, and cedar shake roofs, which offer a classic look for historic homes, require regular maintenance to prevent leaks. The inspection's condition rating, not age alone, should drive the call.

Roof repairs address leaks, missing shingles, and weather damage, while full roof replacements suit aging or storm-damaged roofs. When replacement is right, Newark Quality Roofing quotes the roof replacement or new roof installation in writing, in asphalt shingles, slate, or metal roofing. Architectural shingles can mimic the look of slate or cedar and can carry a manufacturer's 50-year limited warranty, and historic Montclair homes need specialized care that repairs slate, copper, and period detailing in kind.

faqs.q: How often should I have my Montclair roof inspected?

runs.v: The NRCA recommends a roof inspection at least twice per year, spring and fall, plus an additional inspection after any major weather event. A spring inspection follows winter freeze-thaw stress and a fall inspection precedes it, and proper maintenance on that cadence extends asphalt-shingle service life by roughly 25–30%, per ARMA. Montclair's reservation-edge and street-tree canopy adds a post-storm inspection after a branch-impact event.

faqs.q: Can a roof inspection find a leak before it appears inside?

runs.v: Yes. Moisture meters and infrared imaging find wet decking and framing before a stain shows, so a failing flashing or membrane detail on a Montclair home is caught while the repair stays minor.

faqs.q: Does a roof inspection or roofing work in a Montclair historic district need extra approval?

runs.v: An inspection that only documents condition needs no approval. Before roofing work that changes a property's exterior appearance, confirm requirements with the Montclair construction office, because properties in a historic district or designated landmarks can need extra review; per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: What does a Montclair roof inspection report cover?

runs.v: A Newark Quality Roofing report covers roof-covering condition, flashing, drainage, ventilation, sealants, the deck, and active-leak indications, rated by urgency on a roof diagram with photographs, following the InterNACHI roof inspection standard of practice.

faqs.q: How do I choose a roofing contractor in New Jersey?

runs.v: In New Jersey, home improvement contractors must be registered with the Division of Consumer Affairs, so confirm registration and insurance, check the contractor's reputation, and get the price in writing with no hidden fees. A contractor's roof inspection is not a licensed home inspection: New Jersey requires licensed home inspectors to maintain errors and omissions insurance, while Newark Quality Roofing is a registered, insured Home Improvement Contractor.
